title: Dispatch TUR 7: A Platform Rises in the Goods Yard
summary: Volunteers assemble the Westmere terminus as water appears along its unfinished route.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: Work began in the goods yard at dawn, with the council’s order against excavation still in force. Mr. Wren’s platform rests on timber trestles and touches no depot wall. Postal workers brought the original timetable plate. Mrs. Harrow supplied the three red lamps described in Miriam’s letters. Someone hung a board reading ALDERWICK WESTMERE, a name never approved by the old railway company.

Dr. Saye asked volunteers to work from the 1881 plans wherever possible. “We cannot construct thirteen years of railway in a morning,” she told them. “We can make its end unmistakable.” Beneath the platform, water gathered over dry gravel without flowing from any visible pipe.

The council sent officers to stop the work. Alderman Dorne arrived with them, read Pell’s last letter, and withdrew the order. He then helped carry a trestle into place. “I cannot certify this station,” he said. “I can see that it is needed.”

At 6:40 p.m., the newly mounted clock stopped. Though its hands were wound and its mechanism remained intact, they would not pass the departure time on the old timetable. A bell sounded from the empty end of the yard. The receiver in the coal cellar registered a moving signal for seventeen minutes.

Mr. Pike delivered one final envelope to Mrs. Harrow. It contained no letter, only a child’s drawing of the platform completed exactly as the volunteers had built it. In the corner was a figure with a yellow umbrella. Beside her, in different handwriting, someone had added a small boy.
